title: A SHEPHERD'S HEART FOR THE PEOPLE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses said to the LORD, "May the LORD, the God who gives breath to all living things, appoint someone over this community to go out and come in before them, one who will lead them out and bring them in, so the people of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." - Num 27:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having just been told he would not enter the land, Moses' first concern is not for himself but for the people. He asks God to appoint a new leader so that Israel would not be left like sheep without a shepherd. Even at the end of his life, facing his own death, Moses' heart beats for the good of God's people.

What a picture of selfless leadership. Moses could have been consumed with his own disappointment. Instead, he thinks of those he would leave behind, longing that they be well cared for after he is gone. He knew that a flock without a shepherd would scatter and be vulnerable, and he could not bear that thought for the people he had led so long.

This tender concern reflects the very heart of God, who is the true Shepherd of His people. Moses' prayer reveals a leader who loved as God loves, putting the welfare of the flock above his own. Such shepherd-hearted care is precious in God's sight.

And Moses' longing points us to the perfect Shepherd who was to come. When Jesus looked upon the crowds, He too saw them as sheep without a shepherd, and He had compassion on them (Mark 6:34). He is the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep and never leaves them. In Christ, God's people will never truly be shepherdless.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you care for others' welfare even in your own hard times?
2. How does Moses' shepherd-heart reflect the heart of God?
3. What comfort do you find in Jesus, the Good Shepherd?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me a heart like Moses that cares for others even in my own trials. Thank You for Jesus, the Good Shepherd, who never leaves His flock and lays down His life for the sheep. Amen.
